examples: Sit near me.
The park is near the school.
Stay near your mom.

more.def: Not far from a person, place or thing.
examples: Our house is near the beach.
A deer stood near the edge of the woods.
Please stay near me in the crowd.
The beach is near.
The nearest store is far.
Summer is near.

more.def: Not far away in space or in time.
examples: The nearest hospital is ten miles away.
The end of the school year is near.
We will move in the near future.

easy.def: The part of your body between your head and shoulders.
examples: A giraffe has a long neck.
My neck is stiff.
He wore a scarf around his neck.

more.def: The part of the body that joins the head to the shoulders.
examples: A giraffe has a very long neck.
She wore a scarf around her neck.
The cat stretched its neck to see.
I need water.
Plants need sun.
She needs a coat.

more.def: To require something because you cannot do well without it.
examples: Fish need clean water to stay healthy.
We needed more time to finish the puzzle.
Do you need any help with your backpack?

easy.def: A person who lives near you.
examples: My neighbor has a big dog.
Our neighbor gave us cookies.
I wave to my neighbor.

more.def: A person who lives next to or near you.
examples: Our neighbor waters our plants when we are away.
Canada is a neighbor of the United States.
The girl who sits next to me in class is a good neighbor.

easy.def: Not one and not the other.
examples: Neither of us was late.
I like neither.
Neither is correct.

more.def: Not the first one and not the second one.
examples: Neither of my brothers likes spinach.
I have two pens, but neither works.
Neither of us knew the answer.

easy.def: Used with "nor" to say not one and not the other.
examples: Neither Mia nor Sam was late.
It was neither hot nor cold.
He ate neither fish nor meat.

more.def: Used before the first of two choices to say that both are untrue.
examples: Neither the red bike nor the blue one has a bell.
We saw neither deer nor bears on our walk.
It is neither too hot nor too cold.
I feel nervous on the first day of school.
The nervous cat hid under the bed.
I get nervous at the dentist.

more.def: Worried or a little afraid about something that is going to happen.
examples: She felt nervous before her piano recital.
He was nervous about meeting his new teacher.
The nervous horse jumped at every sound.
I never eat fish.
He has never seen snow.
The sun never stops shining.

more.def: At no time, or not even once.
examples: Penguins never fly, but they are excellent swimmers.
I have never been on an airplane before.
She never forgets to feed the fish.

easy.def: Just made, or never used before.
examples: I have new shoes.
This is a new book.
The baby is new.

more.def: Recently made or found, or not seen or used before.
examples: The school has a new playground with a long slide.
We moved to a new town last year.
Scientists found a new kind of frog in the rain forest.

easy.def: Information about something that just happened.
examples: I have good news!
We watched the news on TV.
The news made her smile.

more.def: Information about things that have just happened, in the paper, on TV or from other people.
examples: I have good news; we are going to the beach!
Mom reads the news on her phone every morning.
The news that school was closed made everyone cheer.
Who is next?
I go next.
See you next week.

more.def: Coming right after the present one in time, order, or place.
examples: The next bus will come in ten minutes.
Turn to the next page of your book.
Our neighbors live in the next house.
